word_for_word: भीष्मद्रोणेति
with ‘Bhīṣma and Droṇa’
महीक्षितां पितामहद्रोणराज्ञां च प्रमुखतः संमुखे रथं स्थापयित्वा
having placed the chariot directly before the grandsire Bhīṣma, Droṇa, and the kings, the rulers of the earth
हे पार्थ एतान्कुरून्पश्येत्युवाच
he said: O Pārtha, behold these Kurus
ततः किं प्रवृत्तमित्यत आह
then what happened? to this he says
पितॄन् पितृव्यादीनित्यर्थः
‘fathers’ means paternal uncles and the like
पुत्रान्पौत्रानिति दुर्योधनादीनां ये पुत्राः पौत्राश्च तानित्यर्थः
‘sons and grandsons’ means the sons and grandsons of Duryodhana and the others
सखीन्मित्राणि
‘companions’ means friends
सुहृदः कृतोपकारांश्चापश्यत्
and he saw well-wishers, those who had rendered benefits
ततः किं कृतवानित्यत आह तानिति
then what did he do? to this he says ‘those’
आविष्टो व्याप्तः युक्तः
‘overcome’ means pervaded, possessed
विषीदन्विशेषेण सीदन्नवसादं ग्लानिं लभमानः
‘grieving’ means sinking greatly, obtaining dejection, weariness
किमब्रवीदित्यपेक्षायामाह दृष्ट्वेममित्यादि यावदध्यायसमाप्ति
when it is asked what he said, he states it from ‘seeing this’ to the end of the chapter
हे कृष्ण योद्धुमिच्छन्तं पुरतः सम्यगवस्थितमिमं बन्धुजनं दृष्ट्वा
O Kṛṣṇa, seeing this body of relatives standing properly before me desiring to fight
मदीयानि गात्राणि करचरणादीनि सीदन्ति विशीर्यन्ते
my limbs, hands, feet, and so forth, sink, give way
किंच मुखं परि समंताच्छुष्यति निर्द्रवीभवति
and my mouth dries all around, becomes devoid of moisture
किंच वेपथुश्चेति
and further, with ‘trembling’
वेपथुः कम्पः
‘vepathu’ means trembling
रोमहर्षो रोमाञ्चः
‘romaharṣa’ means horripilation
स्रंसते निपतति
‘slips’ means falls
परिदह्यते सर्वतः संतप्यते
‘burns’ means is heated on every side
अन्यच्च न चेति
and further, with ‘nor’
विपरीतानि निमित्तान्यनिष्टसूचकानि शकुनानि पश्यामि
I see adverse signs, omens indicating what is undesirable
किंच न चेति
and further, with ‘nor’
स्वजनं आहवे युद्धे हत्वा श्रेयः फलं न पश्यामि
I do not see a beneficial result from killing my own people in battle
विजयादिकं फलं किं न पश्यसीति चेत्तत्राह न काङ्क्ष इति
if it is asked, ‘do you not see victory and the like as a result?’ to this he says ‘I do not desire’
एतदेव प्रपञ्चयति किं न इति सार्धाभ्याम्
he expands this very point in the verse and a half beginning ‘of what use?’
यदर्थमस्माकं राज्यादिकमपेक्षितं त एते प्राणधनानि त्यक्त्वा त्यागमङ्गीकृत्य युद्धार्थमवस्थिताः
those for whose sake kingdom and the like are desired by us are these very people, standing for battle after abandoning life and wealth, accepting their relinquishment
अतः किमस्माकं राज्यादिभिः कृत्यमित्यर्थः
therefore what use have we for kingdom and the rest? this is the meaning

ननु यदि कृपया त्वमेतान्न हंसि त्वामेते राज्यलोभेन हनिष्यन्त्येव
objection: if out of compassion you do not kill these men, they themselves will kill you out of greed for the kingdom
अतस्त्वमेवैतान्हत्वा राज्यं भुङ्क्ष्व तत्राह एतान्नेति सार्धेन
therefore you should kill them and enjoy the kingdom; to this he replies in the verse and a half beginning ‘these I do not’
घ्नतोऽप्यस्मान्घातयतोऽप्येतांस्त्रैलोक्यराज्यस्यापि हेतोस्तत्प्राप्त्यर्थमप्यहं हन्तुं नेच्छामि
even if they kill us, even if they cause us to be killed, I do not wish to kill them even for the sovereignty of the three worlds, even for obtaining that

ननु च अग्निदो गरदश्चैव शस्त्रपाणिर्धनापहः क्षेत्रदारापहर्ता च षडेते ह्याततायिनः इति स्मरणात्
objection: according to the Smṛti, ‘the incendiary, poisoner, armed attacker, thief of wealth, usurper of land, and abductor of another’s wife—these six are aggressors’
अग्निद इत्यादिभिः षड्भिरपि हेतुभिरेते तावदाततायिनः
by all six causes beginning with incendiarism, these are indeed aggressors
आततायिनां च वधो युक्त एव
and the killing of aggressors is certainly proper
आततायिनमायान्तं हन्यादेवाविचारयन् नाततायिवधे दोषो हन्तुर्भवति कश्चन इति वचनात्
because it is said: ‘one should kill an approaching aggressor without deliberation; no fault whatsoever belongs to the killer in killing an aggressor’
तत्राह सार्धेन पापमिति
to this he replies in the verse and a half beginning ‘sin’
अततायिनमायान्तम् इत्यादिकमर्थशास्त्रं धर्मशास्त्राद्दुर्बलम्
the Arthaśāstra statement beginning ‘an approaching aggressor’ is weaker than Dharmaśāstra
यथोक्तं याज्ञवल्क्येन स्मृत्योर्विरोधे न्यायस्तु बलवान्व्यवहारतः अर्थशास्त्रात्तु बलवद्धर्मशास्त्रमिति स्थितिः
as Yājñavalkya has said: ‘when two Smṛtis conflict, judicial reasoning is stronger in legal practice; but Dharmaśāstra is stronger than Arthaśāstra—this is the settled rule’
तस्मादाततायिनामप्येतेषामार्यादीनां वधेऽस्माकं पापमेव भवेदन्याय्यत्वादधर्मत्वाच्चैतद्वधस्य
therefore even though these venerable persons and others are aggressors, killing them would be sin for us, because such killing is unjust and contrary to dharma
न चेह सुखं स्यादित्याह स्वजनं हीति
and there would be no happiness here; he says this with ‘for our own people’

objection: since the fault of killing relatives is the same for you and for them, just as they accept that fault and enter battle, so should you; what use is this despondency? to this he replies in the two verses beginning ‘although’
राज्यलोभेनोपहतं भ्रष्टविवेकं चेतो येषां त एते दुर्योधनादयो यद्यपि दोषं न पश्यन्ति
although these men, Duryodhana and the others, whose minds are struck by greed for the kingdom and whose discrimination is ruined, do not see the fault
